[[Renfrew]], [[Scotland]] | key_people = [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] Andy Colquhoun | industry = [[Energy industry|Energy services]] | num_employees = 5,414 (2008) | parent = {{ubl|Independent {{smaller|(1891–1987)}}|FKI Babcock PLC {{smaller|(1987–89)}}|[[Babcock International|Babcock Intl. Group]] {{smaller|(1989–95)}}|[[Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding|Mitsui]] {{smaller|(1995–2006)}}|[[Doosan Group]] {{smaller|(2006–22)}}|Altrad {{smaller|(2022–present)}}}} | successors = {{ubl|[https://altradbabcock.com/ Altrad Babcock Ltd.]}} | website = https://altradbabcock.com/ }} '''Altrad Babcock Ltd''' (formerly '''Doosan Babcock Ltd.''') is a power sector [[original equipment manufacturer]] (OEM), construction, upgrade, and after-market services company that offers specialist services and technologies to the [[fossil fuel power station|fossil-fired power]] generation, [[nuclear power]] generation, and [[petroleum industry|oil, gas, and petrochemical industries]]. AB's main headquarters are in [[Crawley]], [[England]]. European headquarters are in [[Renfrew]], [[Scotland]]. The company has manufacturing facilities in the [[United Kingdom|UK]], [[Germany]], [[India]], [[Vietnam]] and [[South Korea]], and 17 offices around the world.{{cite web|url=http://www.doosanpowersystems.com/assets/Documents/OilGasPetrochemical.pdf?1381745130 |title=Doosan Babcock Oil, Gas and Petrochemical |publisher=Doosan Babcock Limited |year=2013 |website=Doosan Power Systems |format=PDF |accessdate=18 November 2013 }}{{dead link|date=January 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} The company began as [[Babcock International|Babcock & Wilcox Ltd]] founded in 1891 by the American [[Babcock & Wilcox]] company. The boiler manufacturing and energy services division of Babcock International were later sold off to Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding of Japan. After acquiring it from Mitsui in 2006, Doosan Heavy Industries & Construction sold the company to Altrad in 2022. After the purchase by Altrad was completed in September 2022, DB was renamed Altrad Babcock.{{Cite news|url=https://www.altrad.com/en/newsreader/altrad-completes-the-acquisition-of-doosan-babcock-limited.html/|title=Altrad completes the acquisition of Doosan Babcock Limited|work=Altrad|access-date=2022-12-21|language=en-US}} ==Company products and services== ===Thermal=== Doosan Babcock provides a range of through-life services to the thermal power industry, including project design and construction, plant maintenance, asset integrity, shutdown/turnaround management, plant life extension and upgrades. The company provides OEM boilers to power plants burning traditional and renewable fuels, plus a range of firing technologies, subcritical or supercritical systems and unit sizes from 100MW to 660MW and above. It has a license agreement with [[Harbin Electric|Harbin Boiler]], the largest boiler maker in China. Doosan Babcock is the developer of the thermal OxyCoalTM [[Oxy-fuel combustion process|oxy-fuel]] boiler, used at the [[Schwarze Pumpe power station|Vattenfall Oxyfuel pilot plant in Schwarze Pumpe]] in Germany. Oxy-fuel boilers use pure oxygen rather than air as the primary oxidant to reduce fuel consumption and emissions.{{cite web |url = http://www.powerplantccs.com/ccs/cap/con/of/of.html |title=Power Plant Combustion Method |year=2010 |website=Power Plant CSS |accessdate=18 November 2013}} The company is active in the [[carbon capture and storage]] sector and was responsible for designing, building and commissioning the UK's largest carbon capture pilot plant in [[Ferrybridge power stations|Ferrybridge]], West Yorkshire, which began operations in November 2011. The project, which uses the company's advanced amine scrubbing technology is a collaboration between [[SSE plc|SSE]], Doosan Babcock and [[Vattenfall]], and is the first of its size to be integrated into a live power plant in the UK.{{cite web|url=http://www.sse.com/uploadedFiles/Z_Microsites/Ferrybridge/Controls/Lists/Resources/CCPilot100+Brochure.pdf |title=CC Pilot100+ |year=2013 |website=SSE |accessdate=18 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810071603/http://www.sse.com/uploadedFiles/Z_Microsites/Ferrybridge/Controls/Lists/Resources/CCPilot100+Brochure.pdf |archivedate=10 August 2014 }} ===Nuclear=== Doosan Babcock has been a major supplier of specialist services to the nuclear industry for around 60 years, since it built the steam raising plant for the world's first commercial nuclear power station, [[Calder Hall nuclear power station|Calder Hall UK]], in 1956.{{cite news|title=Calder Hall Power Station No. 1 |pages=464–467 |newspaper=The Engineer |date=31 August 1998 |url=http://www.theengineer.co.uk/journals/pdf/21835.pdf |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029195328/http://www.theengineer.co.uk/journals/pdf/21835.pdf |archivedate=2013-10-29 }} Approximately 3500 [[SQEP|Suitably Qualified and Experienced Personnel (SQEP)]] offer [[Engineering, procurement, and construction|engineering, procurement and construction (EPC)]], plant maintenance and [[Nuclear decommissioning|decommissioning]] services to the nuclear power industry in the form of specialist support teams, bespoke projects and turnkey solutions. The company has a presence at every nuclear power generating site in the UK.{{cite web|url=http://www.doosanpowersystems.com/assets/Documents/Nuclear.pdf?1381745288 |title=Nuclear. New Build and Operational Support |year=2011 |website=Doosan Power Systems |format=PDF |accessdate=18 November 2013 }}{{dead link|date=January 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} As a specialist provider of nuclear decommissioning services, Doosan Babcock has managed decommissioning projects at sites around the UK, including [[Sellafield]],{{cite web |url = http://suppliers.sellafieldsites.com/supplier/doosan-power-systems-limited/ |title=Suppliers |year=2013 |website=Sellafield |accessdate=18 November 2013}} [[HMNB Clyde|Faslane]]{{cite web |last=Fisher |first=Paul |url=http://www.scottish-enterprise.com/~/media/SE/Resources/Documents/DEF/Doosan-Babcock-Decom-Aberdeen.pdf |title=Doosan Babcock Overview of Two Decommissioning Projects |publisher=Doosan Power Systems |date=23 March 2011 |website=Scottish Enterprise |accessdate=18 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610222207/http://www.scottish-enterprise.com/~/media/SE/Resources/Documents/DEF/Doosan-Babcock-Decom-Aberdeen.pdf |archive-date=10 June 2015 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }} and [[Bradwell nuclear power station|Bradwell]].{{cite web|url=http://www.doosanpowersystems.com/NewsEvents/News/2013-08-14/Doosan-Babcock-achieves-early-milestone-in-Bradwell-deplanting/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131119160903/http://www.doosanpowersystems.com/NewsEvents/News/2013-08-14/Doosan-Babcock-achieves-early-milestone-in-Bradwell-deplanting/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 November 2013 |title=Doosan Babcock achieves early milestone in Bradwell deplanting |date=14 August 2013 |website=Doosan Power Systems |accessdate=18 November 2013 }} The company offers techniques and processes for the removal of radioactive waste and the remediation of nuclear facilities. It is at the forefront of waste encapsulation technologies.{{cite web|url=http://www.engineerlive.com/content/23447 |title=Polymeric encapsulation for radioactive waste immobilisation |website=Engineer Live |accessdate=18 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328071449/http://engineerlive.com/content/23447 |archivedate=28 March 2014 }} ===Oil, gas and petrochemical=== Doosan Babcock provides project design and construction, plant maintenance, asset integrity assessment, shutdown/turnaround management, plant life extension and upgrade services to the global oil, gas and petrochemical industry. The company's oil, gas and petrochemical clients include [[BP]], [[Equinor]], [[Royal Dutch Shell|Shell]], Essar, Total, [[ConocoPhillips]], [[ExxonMobil]], [[SABIC]] and Nippon Gohsei. ===Technologies=== Doosan Babcock develops and manufactures proprietary safety assessment tools such as the pipe vibration meter,{{cite web|url=http://www.pipevibrationmeter.co.uk/ |title=The Pipe Vibration Meter (PVM) |website=Pipe Vibration Meter |accessdate=18 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220125408/http://www.pipevibrationmeter.co.uk/ |archivedate=20 December 2013 }} a hazardous area logger and a pipe reeling test rig, and can repair and replace plant components in large workshops in Europe and Asia. The company also deploys a range of asset integrity assessment technologies, which include non-destructive testing, laser 3D scanning and remote visual inspection. ==Safety record and awards== Doosan Babcock achieved eight million man-hours without a [[Occupational injury|lost time incident (LTI)]] at [[Grangemouth Refinery|INEOS Grangemouth]] in Scotland and 10 million man-hours without an LTI on an emissions-reduction project at [[Castle Peak Power Station]] in Hong Kong. In 2013 the company was presented with the ExxonMobil Fawley Site Contractor Safety Award and the British Safety Council's Sword of Honour {{cite web|url=https://www.britsafe.org/sites/default/files//editor/SOH%202013%20winners%20list.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141122090456/https://www.britsafe.org/sites/default/files//editor/SOH%202013%20winners%20list.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 November 2014 |title=Sword of Honour Winners 2013 |website=British Safety Council |accessdate=18 November 2013 }} for best practices in Health and Safety. In 2012 Doosan Babcock completed over 36,000 field welds with a 99.88% success rate. The Grangemouth site in the east of Scotland, recently achieved 12 million man hours without a lost time incident (LTI). This helped them achieve the prestigious British Safety Council's Sword of Honour in 2017, which was awarded to them in London. ==History== [[File:Babcock & Wilcox Limited - Works - Renfrew - Scotland - circa 1919.jpeg|thumb|Babcock & Wilcox Limited works, [[Renfrew]] circa 1919]] The US [[Babcock & Wilcox|Babcock & Wilcox Company]] opened an office in Glasgow, Scotland in 1881. B & W commenced boiler making with and in the Singer Manufacturing Company works at Clydebank, initially using components shipped from the US. In 1891, Babcock & Wilcox formed a British company named '''Babcock & Wilcox Ltd'''.{{cite web|url=http://www.nahste.ac.uk/cgi-bin/view_isad.pl?id=GB-0248-UGD-309&view=basic |title=Records of Babcock International Group plc |website=NAHSTE |accessdate=18 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120714222855/http://www.nahste.ac.uk/cgi-bin/view_isad.pl?id=GB-0248-UGD-309&view=basic |archivedate=14 July 2012 }} The board members include renowned Scottish structural engineer [[William Arrol]] and Andrew Stewart, of the Lanarkshire-based steel tubemakers A & J Stewart and Menzies, subsequently [[Stewarts & Lloyds]]. A manufacturing facility at Renfrew, Scotland based on the existing Porterfield Foundry was established in 1895 In 1956, Babcock & Wilcox supplied the steam raising plant for the world's first commercial nuclear power station, [[Calder Hall nuclear power station|Calder Hall]] in the UK. Babcock Power Ltd established in 1979; later renamed Babcock Energy Ltd. Babcock Energy Ltd was floated on the stock exchange in 1982, becoming Babcock International PLC. In 1987 Babcock International entered a short-lived merger with FKI Electricals, forming '''FKI Babcock PLC'''. In 1989, FKI Babcock PLC demerged to form [[Babcock International|Babcock International Group PLC]] and [[FKI (company)|FKI PLC]].{{cite web |url=http://www.archives.gla.ac.uk/collects/catalog/ugd/301-350/ugd309-24.html |title=Records of Babcock Industrial & Electrical Products Ltd |website=University of Glasgow Archive Services |accessdate=18 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070310191355/http://www.archives.gla.ac.uk/collects/catalog/ugd/301-350/ugd309-24.html |archivedate=10 March 2007 }} In 1995, a 75% stake in Babcock's boiler manufacturing and energy services activities (known as Babcock Energy Ltd) was sold to [[Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding]] of Japan, to become Mitsui Babcock Energy Ltd.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukbusinesspark.co.uk/babcocka.htm |title=UK Activity Report - Babcock |website=UK Business Park |accessdate=18 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616093637/http://www.ukbusinesspark.co.uk/babcocka.htm |archivedate=16 June 2013 }} Babcock Energy Ltd provides the steam generators for the British [[Sizewell nuclear power stations|Sizewell B]] nuclear power station. Mitsui sold Babcock Energy Ltd to [[Doosan Enerbility|Doosan Heavy Industries & Construction]], a subsidiary company of the [[Doosan Group]] of South Korea in 2006. The UK company is renamed Doosan Babcock Energy Ltd.{{cite web|url=http://www.nce.co.uk/mitsui-babcock-sold-to-doosan-heavy-industries-of-south-korea/66770.article |title=Mitsui to sell Mitsui Babcock to South Korean Firm |website=Antara |accessdate=18 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120819141557/http://www.nce.co.uk/mitsui-babcock-sold-to-doosan-heavy-industries-of-south-korea/66770.article |archivedate=August 19, 2012 }} In 2010, Doosan Babcock Energy Ltd renamed [[Doosan Power Systems|Doosan Power Systems Ltd]], then in 2012 renamed Doosan Power Systems UK Ltd. In 2013, Doosan Power Systems UK Ltd renamed as Doosan Babcock Ltd. The same year Doosan Babcock Ltd invested £20 million in UK test facility and research and development activities. New offices opened in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * {{Official website|https://altradbabcock.com/}} {{Doosan Group}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Engineering companies of the United Kingdom]] [[Category:Companies based in Crawley]] [[Category:Renfrew]] [[Category:2006 mergers and acquisitions]] [[Category:2022 mergers and acquisitions]]
